what: added a PRESERVE channel to assurance/_repair.py's selftest and mutation-tested it
channel: plant stash+breadcrumb, create a file at the LIVE path with no stash counterpart, call repair_full, require the file survives AND the stash still comes home
negative_inline: a move-the-tree variant must destroy it, so the control cannot pass on an implementation that clobbers

negative_first_version_could_not_fail.why: it reused the positive's canary path, which lives INSIDE the campaign dir, so stashing the dir carried the canary along and restoring brought it back; it also deleted ep4.name while checking a path built from ep3.name
negative_first_version_could_not_fail.caught_by: the control itself, reporting FAIL for its own reasons
negative_first_version_could_not_fail.fix: the negative's canary is created AFTER the stash move under its own name

mutation_test.method: temporarily replace repair_full's per-file copy loop with rmtree+move of the whole tree, run --selftest, then
mutation_test.conclusion: the control rejects a broken repair_full, so it tests the FUNCTION and not the inline variant — the instrument-vs-claim unit mismatch that three earlier rounds in this arc turned up does not apply here
mutation_test.restoration_verified: 0 occurrences of the mutation marker remain

summary_count_now_computed: the selftest printed 'all THREE channels'; it now prints len(CHANNELS) and the names, because this file already records that R428's hand-typed 'eight times, on BOTH channels' went stale
evidence_is_run_once: this artifact RECORDS a mutation test performed by hand; no mutating script is shipped, because a script that edits a shared tool is a hazard of exactly the kind R935-R938 were about
live_limitation: the definition describes the instance; one release, one core
